raw:
The task: write UI strings in Traditional Chinese (Taiwan usage) for a settings page reset button.

- s1: button text that resets all options to factory/default values
- s2: confirmation dialog title
- s3: confirmation dialog description sentence

Common Taiwan UI conventions: "還原預設值", "重設為預設值", "回復預設設定". The word "默認" must be "預設". Avoid "重置"? Taiwan often uses "重設" or "還原". Common Microsoft style: "重設為預設值" or "還原預設值". 

s1: "還原預設值" or "重設所有設定". Since the button resets all options to installation defaults: "還原預設值" is good. Perhaps "重設為預設值".

s2: confirmation dialog title: "還原預設值" or "確認還原預設值？"

s3: description: "系統會將所有設定還原為安裝時的初始值，且無法復原。確定要繼續嗎？" Hmm, but if there's a confirm dialog with confirm/cancel, the description could be "所有設定將還原為安裝時的預設值，此操作無法復原。"

Avoid mainland terms: "恢復出廠設置" is more mainland-ish; Taiwan uses "回復原廠設定" actually. "還原" is common in Taiwan (System Restore = 系統還原). "原廠設定" is used in Taiwan for factory reset (手機回復原廠設定). So could use "回復原廠設定" but the context is app settings to installation defaults.

s1: "還原預設值" — good.
s2: "確認還原預設值" or "還原預設值？"
s3: "所有設定將回復為安裝時的預設值，此操作無法復原。確定要繼續嗎？"

Also avoid "點擊" etc. No need. Use "無法復原" or "無法回復". Taiwan: "復原" is common (undo = 復原). "無法復原" fine.

JSON output only.{"s1": "還原預設值", "s2": "確認還原預設值？", "s3": "所有設定將回復為安裝時的預設值，此操作無法復原。確定要繼續嗎？"}

parsed.s3: 所有設定將回復為安裝時的預設值，此操作無法復原。確定要繼續嗎？
